nodes.name: Reduce to Theorem 3
nodes.statement: (1) Proof of Theorem \ref{thm:talagrand_inequality}, we can use Theorem 6.1 in \cite{bousquet2003concentration} and Theorem \ref{thm:bennett_inequality} to get the following:
nodes.statement_short: Apply Bousquet's Theorem 6.1 together with Theorem 3.

nodes.name: Increment bounds
nodes.statement: $ Y_{kjl} \leq Z_{kj}-Z_{kj}^{\backslash \{ l \} } \leq 1$, these inequalities are owing to \begin{align*} & \sum_{i \in I_{kj} \backslash \{l \} } f_l^{kj}({\mathbf{x}}_i) = \sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} \sum_{i \in I_{kj} \backslash \{l \}} f({\mathbf{x}}_i), ~ Y_{kjl} = f_l^{kj}({\mathbf{x}}_l), \\ & Y_{kjl} \leq Z_{kj}-Z_{kj}^{\backslash \{ l \} } \leq f_{kj}^*({\mathbf{x}}_l) \leq 1, ~ \mathbb{E}_{kjl} [Y_{kjl}] = 0. \\ \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Check $Y_{kjl} \le Z_{kj}-Z_{kj}^{\setminus l} \le 1$ with zero conditional mean.

nodes.name: Variance condition
nodes.statement: $\sigma_{kj}^2 \geq \sum_{l \in I_{kj}} \mathbb{E} _{I_{kj}} [Y_{kjl}^2]$, because \begin{align*} \sum_{l \in I_{kj}} \mathbb{E} _{I_{kj}} [Y_{kjl}^2] = \sum_{l \in I_{kj}} \mathbb{E} _{I_{kj}} [f_l^{{kj}^2}({\mathbf{x}}_l)] \leq \sum_{l \in I_{kj}} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} \mathbb{E} [f^2 {\mathbf{x}}_l)]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Check the variance proxy condition $\sigma_{kj}^2 \ge \sum_l E[Y_{kjl}^2]$.

nodes.name: Define constants
nodes.statement: Define some constants as follows: \begin{align*} & \sigma^2 = \sum_{k \in [K]} \sum_{j \in [J_k]} \omega_{kj} \sigma_{kj}^2, \ v = (1 + b) \mathbb{E} [Z] + \sigma^2, c = \frac{5^2}{4^2} \sum_{k \in [K]} \chi_{f} (G_k), \ \chi_{f} (G_k) \overset{\textup{def}}{=} \sum_{j \in [J_k]} \omega_{kj} , \\ & p_k = \frac{U_k}{U}, q_{kj} = \frac{\omega_{kj} \max (1, \overbrace{v_{kj}^{\frac{1}{2}} W^{\frac{1}{2}} v^{-\frac{1}{2}} } ^{\triangle})}{U_k}, U = \sum_{k \in [K]} U_k, U_k = \sum_{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \max(1, \triangle), \\ & W = \sum_{k \in [K]} \chi_f(G_k) = \sum_{k \in [K]} \omega_k, \sigma _k^2 = \sum_{j \in I_{J_k}} \omega_{kj} \sigma _{kj}^2, \omega_k = \sum_{j \in [J_k]} \omega_{kj}, v_k = \sum_{j \in [J_k]} \omega_{kj}v_{kj} = (1+b) \mathbb{E} [Z_k] +\sigma _k^2. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $\sigma^2, v, c, p_k, q_{kj}, U, W$.

nodes.name: Chernoff-Jensen bound
nodes.statement: Then \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}(Z-\mathbb{E} Z \geq t) & = \mathbb{P}(e^{\lambda (Z- \mathbb{E} Z)} \geq e^{\lambda t}) \overset{\text{\ding{172}}}{\leq} \underbrace{ \mathbb{E}(e^{\lambda (Z- \mathbb{E} Z)}) }_{e^{G(\lambda )}} \cdot e^{-\lambda t}. \\ G(\lambda ) & = \log \mathbb{E} (e^{\lambda (Z - \mathbb{E} Z)}) \\ & = \log \mathbb{E} (e^{\lambda \sum _{k \in [K]}p_k \frac{1}{p_k} (Z_k - \mathbb{E} _{X_k} [Z_k] )}) \\ & = \log \mathbb{E} (e^{\lambda \sum _{k \in [K]}p_k \frac{1}{p_k} \sum _{j \in [J_k] } q_{kj} \frac{\omega_{kj}}{q_{kj}} (Z_{kj} - \mathbb{E} _{X_{I_{kj}}} [Z_{kj}] )}) \\ & \overset{\text{\ding{173}}}{\leq} \log \sum_{k \in [K]}p_k\sum_{j \in [J_k]}q_{kj} \mathbb{E}(e^{\frac{\lambda \omega_{kj}}{p_k q_{kj}}(Z_{kj}- \mathbb{E} [Z_{kj}]) }) ,\\ G_{kj}(\lambda ) & = \log \mathbb{E} (e^{\lambda (Z_{kj}- \mathbb{E} Z_{kj})}), \\ G(\lambda ) & \overset{\text{\ding{174}}}{\leq} \log \sum_{k \in [K]}p_k\sum_{j \in [J_k]}q_{kj} (e^{ G_{kj} ({\frac{\lambda \omega_{kj}}{p_k q_{kj}} })}) \\ & \overset{\text{\ding{175}}}{\leq} \log \sum_{k \in [K]}p_k\sum_{j \in [J_k]}q_{kj} (e^{ v_{kj} \psi (-{\frac{\lambda \omega_{kj}}{p_k q_{kj}} })}). \end{align*} \text{\ding{172}} is due to the Markov Inequality, i.e., $\mathbb{P} [x > a] \leq \frac{\mathbb{E}[x]}{a}$, and we define $e^{G(\lambda) } = \mathbb{E} (e^{\lambda (Z - \mathbb{E} Z)}) $. \text{\ding{173}} is due to the Jensen inequality, and \text{\ding{174}} is due to the assumption \ref{thm:assump1}, the last inequality \text{\ding{175}} is due to Theorem 1 \cite{bousquet2002bennett,bousquet2003concentration}, i.e., $G(\lambda) \leq \psi(-\lambda)v $). We can observe that $ v_{kj} \psi (-{\frac{\lambda \omega_{kj}}{p_k q_{kj}} }) \leq \frac{v}{W} \psi (-\lambda U)$ (proof in Lemma~\ref{pro: inequality technique}), then we have \begin{align} \mathbb{P}(Z-\mathbb{E} Z \geq t) \leq e^{\frac{v}{W} \psi (-\lambda U) - \lambda t}, \end{align} we solve the minimum optimization problem with respect to $\lambda$, for $\lambda = \frac{ln(1+\frac{tW}{vU})}{U}$, then \begin{align} \mathbb{P} (Z- \mathbb{E} Z \geq t) \leq e^{-\frac{v}{W} \varphi (\frac{tW}{vU})}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Markov, Jensen over convex weights and Bousquet's bound give $P \le e^{-\frac{v}{W}\varphi(\frac{tW}{vU})}$.

nodes.name: Bound U by 5W/4
nodes.statement: Then \begin{align*} U_k & = \sum _{j \in [J_k]} w_{kj} \max (1, \triangle) \\ & \overset{\text{\ding{172}}}{\leq} \sum _{j \in [J_k]} w_{kj} (1 + \frac{v_{kj} W}{4 v}) = w_k + \frac{v_k W}{4v}, \\ U & = \sum _{k \in [K]} U_k = \sum _{k \in [K]} (w_k + \frac{v_k W}{4v}) = W + \frac{W}{4} = \frac{5}{4}W, \end{align*} \text{\ding{172}} is according to the fact that $\forall x \in \mathbb{R},x \leq 1 + \frac{x^2}{4}$, i.e., $\max (1, \triangle) \leq 1 + \frac{v_{kj} W}{4v}$. Thus \begin{align*} \mathbb{P} (Z \geq \mathbb{E}[Z] & + t) \leq \exp \left( -\frac{v}{W} \varphi \left( \frac{tW}{Uv}\right) \right) \notag \\ \leq \exp & \left( - \frac{v}{ \sum_{k \in [K]} \chi_{f} (G_k)} \varphi \left( \frac{4t}{5v}\right) \right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use $x \le 1+x^2/4$ to get $U \le \frac54 W$.

nodes.name: Bernstein form
nodes.statement: Since $x \geq 0, \varphi (x) \geq \frac{x^2}{2+\frac{2x}{3} } $, inequality (\eqref{eq:thm_bennet_2}) is deduced.
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound $\varphi$ to deduce the Bernstein-type inequality.

nodes.name: Unit weights and constants
nodes.statement: Because of $\omega_{kj}=1$, we can get $\omega_k = |J_k| \in [1,m_k]$, every ${\mathbf{x}}_{kj}$ in only one independent set. Then we can define $p_k,q_{kj}$ and some constants as the following: \begin{align*} & \sigma^2 = \sum_{k \in [K]} \sum_{j \in [J_k]} \omega_{kj} \sigma_{kj}^2, \ v = (1 + b) \mathbb{E} [Z] + \sigma^2, p_k = \frac{U_k}{U}, U = \sum _{k \in [K]} U_k, \\ & c = \sum_{k \in [K]} \chi_{f} (G_k), \ \chi_{f} (G_k) \overset{\textup{def}}{=} \sum_{j \in [J_k]} \omega_{kj}, q_{kj} = \frac{1}{U_k}, U_k = \sum _{j \in [J_k]} = \omega_k . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: With unit weights define $p_k, q_{kj}$ and constants.

nodes.name: Reuse Theorem 3 bound
nodes.statement: Review the proof of the Theorem \ref{thm:bennett_inequality}, we can get: \begin{align} \mathbb{P} (Z - \mathbb{E} Z \geq t) \leq e^{(\log \sum _{k \in [K]} p_k \sum _{j \in [J_k]} q_{kj} (v_{kj} \psi (-\frac{\lambda}{p_k q_{kj}})) - \lambda t)}, \end{align} then \begin{align*} v_{kj} \psi (-\frac{\lambda}{p_k q_{kj}}) = v_{kj} \psi (- \lambda U) \overset{\text{\ding{172}}}{\leq} v \psi (- \lambda U), \end{align*} the inequality \text{\ding{172}} is due to every $v_{kj} \geq 0$, $v = \sum _{k \in [K]} \sum _{j \in [J_k]} v_{kj} \geq v_{kj} $.
nodes.statement_short: Reuse the MGF bound of Theorem 3 and bound $v_{kj} \le v$.

nodes.name: Optimize lambda
nodes.statement: Then the inequality \eqref{equ: bunnet_refined} can be written as the following: \begin{align*} \mathbb{P} (Z - \mathbb{E} Z \geq t) \leq e^{v \psi(- \lambda U) - \lambda t}. \end{align*} We solve the minimum optimization problem with respect to $\lambda$, for $\lambda = \frac{\ln (1 + \frac{t}{v U})}{U}$, then \begin{align*} \mathbb{P} (Z - \mathbb{E} Z \geq t) \leq e^{-v \varphi (\frac{t}{v U})}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Optimize over $\lambda$ to get $e^{-v\varphi(t/(vU))}$.

nodes.name: Identify U = W
nodes.statement: Since $U = \sum _{k \in [K]} U_k = \sum _{k \in [K]} \omega _k = W $, and we noticed $W = \sum _{k \in [K]} \chi_f (G_k)$. Finally, we can get the one part in Theorem \ref{thm:bennett_inequality_refined}, and the second part in Theorem \ref{thm:bennett_inequality_refined} is due to the fact $x \geq 0$, $\varphi (x) \geq \frac{x^2}{2 + \frac{2x}{3}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Use $U = W$ and the lower bound on $\varphi$ to conclude both parts.

nodes.name: Symmetrize and apply Theorem 4
nodes.statement: We can define some variables, $V^+ = \sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} (P f - P_m f)$, $\mathcal{F}_r = \{f, f \in \mathcal{F}, \mathrm{var}(f_k) \leq r\}$, and $f = \sum _{k \in [K]} \sum _{j \in [J_k]} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} f_k({\mathbf{x}}_i) $. then \begin{align*} V^+ = \sup _{f \in \mathcal{F}_r} (P f - P _m f) & = \sup _{f \in \mathcal{F}_r} \mathbb{E} _{{\mathbf{x}}'} [ (\frac{1}{K} \sum _{k \in [K]} \sum _{j \in [J_k]} \frac{\omega_{kj}}{m_k} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} f_k({\mathbf{x}}'_i) - \frac{1}{K} \sum _{k \in [K]} \sum _{j \in J_{k}} \frac{\omega_{kj}}{m_k} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} f_k({\mathbf{x}}_i))] \\ & \leq \mathbb{E} _{{\mathbf{x}}'} [ \sup _{f \in \mathcal{F}_r} (\frac{1}{K} \sum _{k \in [K]} \sum _{j \in [J_k]} \frac{\omega_{kj}}{m_k} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} f_k({\mathbf{x}}'_i) - \frac{1}{K} \sum _{k \in [K]} \sum _{j \in J_{k}} \frac{\omega_{kj}}{m_k} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} f_k({\mathbf{x}}_i)) ] \\ & = \mathbb{E} _{{\mathbf{x}}'} [ \sup _{f \in \mathcal{F}_r} (\frac{1}{K} \sum _{k \in [K]} \sum _{j \in [J_k]} \frac{\omega_{kj}}{m_k} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} ( f_k({\mathbf{x}}'_i) - f_k({\mathbf{x}}_i) ) ], \\ \end{align*} which has differences bounded by $ \frac{1}{K m_k} $ in the sense of the Z in Theorem \ref{thm:talagrand_inequality}, then with probability at least $ 1 - e^{-t}$, \begin{align} V^+ \leq \mathbb{E} V^+ + \frac{1}{K} \sqrt{2cvt} + \frac{2ct}{3K}, \end{align} where $ c = \frac{5^2}{4^2} \sum _{k \in [K]} \frac{\chi _f(G_k)}{m_k}$ and $ v = \sum _{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum _{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \sigma _{kj}^2 +2K\mathbb{E} V^+ \leq Kr + 2K\mathbb{E} V^+ $.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $V^+$, bound it by a ghost-sample supremum and apply Theorem 4.

nodes.name: Simplify and symmetrize
nodes.statement: Then \begin{align*} V^+ & \leq \mathbb{E} V^+ + \sqrt{\frac{2c(r + 2\mathbb{E} V^+) t}{K}} +\frac{2ct}{3K} \\ & \overset{\text{\ding{172}}}{\leq} \mathbb{E} V^+ +\sqrt {\frac{4c \mathbb{E} V^+ t}{K}} + \sqrt {\frac{2crt}{K}} + \frac{2ct}{3K} \\ & \overset{\text{\ding{173}}}{\leq} (1+\alpha) \mathbb{E} V^+ + \sqrt {\frac{2crt}{K}} + (\frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{\alpha})\frac{ct}{K} \\ & \overset{\text{\ding{174}}}{\leq} 2(1 + \alpha) \mathcal{R} (\mathcal{F} , r) + \sqrt {\frac{2crt}{K}} + (\frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{\alpha})\frac{ct}{K}, \\ \end{align*} where \text{\ding{172}} is due to the fact $\sqrt{a + b} \leq \sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b}$, i.e., $\sqrt{\frac{2c(r + 2\mathbb{E} V^+) t}{K}} \leq \sqrt {\frac{4c \mathbb{E} V^+ t}{K}} + \sqrt {\frac{2crt}{K}} $, and \text{\ding{173}} is due to the fact $\forall \alpha > 0, 2 \sqrt{ab} \leq \frac{a}{\alpha} + \alpha b$, and we can combine similar items. \text{\ding{174}} is due to the proposition \ref{pro: equ Rademacher}.
nodes.statement_short: Use $\sqrt{a+b} \le \sqrt a + \sqrt b$, AM-GM and Proposition 1 to reach the stated bound.

nodes.name: Rescaled class G_r
nodes.statement: We can define $\mathcal{G}_r = \{ g = (g_1,g_2,... ,g_K), g_k = \frac{r}{w(f_k)}f_k, f \in \mathcal{F} \} $, $\mathcal{F}(x,y): = \{ f \in \mathcal{F}, T(f_k) \in [x,y] \} $, where $w(f_k) = \min \{r\lambda ^a, a \in \mathbb{N}, r\lambda ^a \geq T(f_k), f \in \mathcal{F} \}$, $V_r^+ = \sup _{g \in \mathcal{G}_r} (P g - P _m g)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the rescaled class $\mathcal{G}_r$ and $V_r^+$.

nodes.name: Variance of G_r
nodes.statement: We can notice $\frac{r}{w(f_k)} \in [0,1]$, then for each $g \in \mathcal{G}_r, \| g_k\|_ \infty \leq 1$, and we found $\mathrm{var}(g_k) \leq r$. Because \begin{itemize} \item $T(f_k) \leq r$, then \begin{align*} a = 0, w(f) = 1, \forall g \in \mathcal{G}_r, g = f , \mathrm{var}(g_k) = \mathrm{var}(f_k) \leq r; \end{align*} \item $T(f_k) >r$, then \begin{align*} g = \frac{f}{\lambda^a}, T(f_k) \in (r \lambda^{a-1}, r\lambda^a], \mathrm{var}(g_k) = \frac{\mathrm{var}(f_k)}{\lambda^{2a}} \leq r. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Show every $g \in \mathcal{G}_r$ has variance at most $r$, by two cases.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Then we can apply Theorem \ref{thm:the core 2.1} for $\mathcal{G}_r$, for all $x > 0$, with probability $1 - e^{-t}$, \begin{align*} V_r^+ \leq 2(1+\alpha) \mathcal{R}(\mathcal{G}_r) +\sqrt{\frac{2crt}{K}} + (\frac{2}{3} +\frac{1}{\alpha}) \frac{ct}{K}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 1 to $\mathcal{G}_r$.

nodes.name: LFRC of G_r
nodes.statement: Then \begin{align*} \mathcal{R}(\mathcal{G}_r) = \frac{1}{K} \left[ \mathbb{E}_ {\mathbf{x}} \mathbb{E} _\zeta \underbrace{ \sup _{g \in \mathcal{G}_r,\mathrm{var}(g_k) \leq r} \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum_{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_l g_k(x_i) }_\spadesuit \right]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Write out $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{G}_r)$.

nodes.name: Peeling
nodes.statement: Let $T(f_k) \leq Bb$, define $a_0$ to be the smallest integer that $r\lambda^{a_0+1} \geq Bb $ and partition $\mathcal{F}(0,Bb) $, i.e., $\mathcal{F}(0,r) + \mathcal{F}(r\lambda^0,r \lambda^1) +\mathcal{F}(r\lambda^1,r \lambda^2),...(r\lambda^{a_0}, r \lambda^{a_0+1}) $, then \begin{align*} \spadesuit & \leq \sup_{g \in \mathcal{G}_r, T(f_k) \in [0,r]} \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum_{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i g_k(x_i) +\sup _{g \in \mathcal{G}_r, T(f) \in [r,Bb]} \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum_{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i g_k(x_i) \\ & = \sup _{f \in \mathcal{F}(0,r)} \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum_{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i f_k(x_i) + \sup _{f \in \mathcal{F}(r,Bb)} \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum_{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i \frac{r}{w(f_k)} f_k(x_i) \\ & \leq \sup _{f \in \mathcal{F}(0,r)} \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum_{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i f_k(x_i) + \sum _{j=0} ^{a_0} \sup _{f \in \mathcal{F}(r\lambda ^j, r \lambda ^{j+1})} \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum_{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i \frac{r}{r\lambda^j} f_k(x_i) \\ & = \sup _{f \in \mathcal{F}(0,r)} \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum_{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i f_k(x_i) + \sum _{j=0} ^{a_0} \frac{1}{\lambda^j} \sup _{f \in \mathcal{F}(r\lambda ^j, r \lambda ^{j+1})} \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum_{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i f_k(x_i). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Partition by $T(f_k)$ into geometric slices and bound slice by slice.

nodes.name: Sub-root bound on R(G_r)
nodes.statement: Since the property in Definition~\ref{lemma: sub-root def}, i.e., $\forall \gamma \geq 1, \Phi(\gamma r) \leq \sqrt{\gamma} \Phi(r)$, then we can get: \begin{align*} \mathcal{R}(\mathcal{G}_r) & \leq \mathcal{R} \mathcal{F} (0,r) + \sum _{j=0} ^{a_0} \frac{1}{\lambda^j} \mathcal{R} \mathcal{F}(r \lambda^j, r \lambda^{j+1} ) \leq \frac{\Phi(r)}{B} + \frac{1}{B} \sum _{j=1} ^{a_0} \frac{1}{\lambda^j} \Phi (r \lambda^{j+1}) \\ & \leq \frac{\Phi(r)}{B} + \frac{1}{B} \sum _{j=1} ^{a_0} \frac{1}{\lambda^j} \lambda^{\frac{j+1}{2}} \Phi (r) = \frac{\Phi(r)}{B} \left[ 1 + \sqrt{\lambda} \sum _{j=0}^{a_0} \frac{1}{\sqrt{\lambda^j}} \right], \end{align*} then taking $\lambda = 4$, we can get: \begin{align*} \mathcal{R}(\mathcal{G}_r) \leq \frac{5\Phi(r)}{B}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Sub-root scaling gives $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{G}_r) \le 5\Phi(r)/B$ with $\lambda=4$.

nodes.name: Bound via fixed point
nodes.statement: Since the property in Definition~\ref{lemma: sub-root def} and Lemma \ref{lemma:sub-root pro}, i.e., $\Phi(r^*) = r^*$, and $\frac{\Phi(r)}{\sqrt{r}}$ is nonincreasing, thus \begin{align*} V_r^+ & \leq 2(1+\alpha) \frac{5\Phi(r)}{B} +\sqrt{\frac{2crt}{K}} + (\frac{2}{3} +\frac{1}{\alpha}) \frac{ct}{K} \\ & \leq \frac{10(1+\alpha)}{B} \sqrt{r r^*} + \sqrt{\frac{2crt}{K}} + (\frac{2}{3} +\frac{1}{\alpha}) \frac{ct}{K}. \end{align*} Then let $A = \frac{10(1+\alpha)}{B} \sqrt{r^*} + \sqrt{\frac{2ct}{K}} $, $C = (\frac{2}{3} +\frac{1}{\alpha}) \frac{ct}{K} $, thus \begin{align*} V_r^+ \leq A \sqrt{r} + C. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use $\Phi(r) \le \sqrt{r r^*}$ to get $V_r^+ \le A\sqrt r + C$.

nodes.name: Apply Bartlett et al. Lemma 3.8
nodes.statement: Then we can apply lemma 3.8 in \cite{Bartlett_2005}, i.e., if $V_r^+ \leq \frac{r}{\lambda B M }$, then $P f \leq \frac{M}{M-1} P_m f + \frac{r}{\lambda BM}$, where $\lambda = 4$, and use a technique, i.e., $\forall \beta >0 , \sqrt{ab} \leq \frac{1}{2}(\beta a + \frac{b}{\beta})$, then \begin{align*} P f & \leq \frac{M}{M-1} P _m f + \lambda BMA^2 +2C \\ & = \frac{M}{M-1} P _m f + \lambda B M (\frac{100(1+\alpha)^2 r^*}{B^2} + \frac{20(1+\alpha)}{B} \sqrt{\frac{2cr^*t}{K}} + \frac{2ct}{K}) + (\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{\alpha}) \frac{2ct}{K}, \\ & \leq \frac{M}{M-1} P _m f + \lambda B M \left[\frac{100(1+\alpha)^2 r^*}{B^2} + \frac{20(1+\alpha)}{B} \left(\frac{1}{2} ( \frac{5r^*}{B} + \frac{2cBt}{5K}) \right) + \frac{2ct}{K} \right] + (\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{\alpha}) \frac{2ct}{K}, \\ \end{align*} let $\alpha = \frac{1}{10}$, then \begin{align*} P f & = \frac{M}{M-1} P _m f + \lambda B M (\frac{121 r^*}{B^2} + \frac{22}{B} (\frac{cBt}{5K} + \frac{5r^*}{2B}) + \frac{2ct}{K}) + \frac{32}{3} \frac{2ct}{K} \\ & = \frac{M}{M-1} P _m f + \frac{(121+55)\lambda M}{B} r^* + \left( \frac{32 \lambda B M}{5} + \frac{64}{3} \right) \frac{ct}{K} \\ & \leq \frac{M}{M-1} P _m f + \frac{704 M}{B} r^* + (26 BM +22 ) \frac{ct}{K}, \\ \end{align*} where $c = \frac{5^2}{4^2} \sum _{k \in [K]} \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{m_k}$. Let $c_1 = 704$, $c_2 = 26$, then we can get inequality \eqref{eq: thm sub-root 3.3_1}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 3.8 of Bartlett et al. and set $\alpha = 1/10$ to get the constants 704 and 26.

nodes.name: Reverse direction
nodes.statement: In the same way, we can define $V_r^- = \sup _{g \in \mathcal{G}_r} (P _m g - P g)$, and then get \begin{align} P_m f \leq \frac{M}{M-1} P f + \frac{c_1 M}{B} r^* + (c_2 BM +22 ) \frac{ct}{K}, \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The same argument for $V_r^-$ gives the reverse inequality.

nodes.name: Reduce to L1-constrained class
nodes.statement: We can observe that $ \mathcal{R}\{ f \in \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{E} f_k^2 \leq r \} = \mathcal{R}\{ f \in \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{E}(\|f_k\|_2) \leq \sqrt{r} \} \leq \mathcal{R}\{f \in \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{E} (\|f_k\|_1) \leq \sqrt{r}\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the variance constraint to a norm constraint.

nodes.name: Eigen-decomposition split
nodes.statement: Donate $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{F}) \leq \mathcal{R} (\mathcal{F}_{2,1})$, $\mathcal{F}_{2,1} = \{ f = (f_1,f_2,...,f_k), k \in [K], \mathbb{E} (\|f_k\|)_1 \leq \sqrt{r} \}$, and $\mathcal{F}_{k_{2,1}} \{ f_k : {\mathbf{x}} \rightarrow \Theta^T \phi ({\mathbf{x}}), \|\theta_k\|_2 \leq Ma, \mathbb{E}(\|f_k\|_1) \leq \sqrt{r} \}$. Then we fix $d = (d_1,d_2,...,d_K)$, \begin{align*} & \frac{1}{K} \sum _{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum _{j \in [J_k]} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i < \theta_k, \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_i)> \\ = & \sum _{k \in [K]} \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{j \in [J_k]} \frac{\omega_{kj}}{\chi_f(G_k)} \sum _{i \in [I_{kj}]} \zeta_i <\theta_k, \phi({\mathbf{x}}_i)> \\ = & \sum _{k \in [K]} <\theta_k, \frac{\chi _f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{j \in [J_k]} \frac{\omega_{kj}}{\chi _f(G_k)} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_i)> \\ \leq & \sum _{k \in [K]} <\theta_k, \frac{\chi _f(G_k)}{K m_k} \zeta_k \phi({\mathbf{x}}_k) > \\ = & \sum _{k \in [K]} [ <\sum _{l = 1}^{d_k} \sqrt{\lambda _{kl}}<\theta_k, \varphi _{kl}>\varphi _{kl} , \sum _{l = 1}^{d_k} \frac{1}{\sqrt{ \lambda _{kl}}} <\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k) , \varphi _{kl} > \varphi _{kl}> \\ + & <\theta_k, \sum _{l > d_k} <\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _{kl} >, \varphi _{kl}>] \\ \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Fix $d$ and split the feature expansion into head and tail eigencomponents.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz on both parts
nodes.statement: Let $\diamondsuit = \frac{1}{K} \sum _{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum _{j \in [J_k]} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i <\theta_k, \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_i)> $, \begin{align*} \mathbb{E} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} (\diamondsuit) & \leq \sup_{ \|\theta_k\|_2 \leq Ma } \sum _{k \in [K]} \sqrt{(\sum _{l=1}^{d_k} \lambda_{kl} <\theta_k, \varphi _{kl}>^2) (\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{l=1}^{d_k} \frac{1}{\lambda _{kl}} \mathbb{E} [< \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _{kl}>^2])} \\ & + \|\theta_k\|_2 \sqrt{\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum_{l > d_k} \mathbb{E}[ < \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _{kl}>^2 ]}, \\ \end{align*} since $\sum _{l=1}^{d_k} \lambda_{kl} <\theta_k, \varphi _l>^2 \leq r$, $\mathbb{E} [< \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _{kl}>^2] = \lambda_{kl}$, then \begin{align*} \mathbb{E} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} (\diamondsuit) \leq \sum _{k \in [K]} \sqrt{\frac{r d_k \chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k}} + \widetilde{M} \sqrt{\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{l > d_k} \lambda _{kl} }.\\ \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound both parts by Cauchy-Schwarz using $E\langle\zeta\phi,\varphi_l\rangle^2 = \lambda_l$.

nodes.name: Minimize over d
nodes.statement: So $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{F}) \leq \mathcal{F}_{2,1} \leq \sum _{k \in [K]} \min _{d_k \geq 0} \sqrt{\frac{r d_k \chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k}} + \widetilde{M} \sqrt{\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{l > d_k} \lambda _{kl}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Take the minimum over $d_k$.

nodes.name: Eigen-decomposition as in Proposition 2
nodes.statement: We can use a similar method (eigenvalue decomposition) to the Proposition \ref{thm:kernel upper bound}, then \begin{align*} & \frac{1}{K} \sum _{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum _{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i < \theta_k, \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_i)> \\ \leq & \sum _{k \in [K]} [ < \sum _{l = 1}^{d} \sqrt{\lambda _{l}}<\theta_k, \varphi _{l}>\varphi _{l} , \sum _{l = 1}^{d} \frac{1}{\sqrt{ \lambda _{l}}} <\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k) , \varphi _{l} > \varphi _{l} > \\ + & < \theta_k, \sum _{l > d} <\frac{1}{K m_k} \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _{l} >, \varphi _{l} > ]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split the expansion as in Proposition 2 with a shared kernel.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz across tasks
nodes.statement: Let $\Box = \frac{1}{K} \sum _{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum _{j \in J_k} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i < \theta_k, \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_i)>$, then \begin{align*} \mathbb{E} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} (\Box) & \leq \sup_{ \|\theta_k\|_2 \leq Ma } \sum _{k \in [K]} \sqrt{(\sum _{l=1}^{d} \lambda_l <\theta_k, \varphi _l>^2) (\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{l=1}^{d} \frac{1}{\lambda _l} \mathbb{E} [< \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _l>^2])} \\ & + \|\theta_k\|_2 \sqrt{\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum_{l > d} \mathbb{E}[ < \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _l>^2 ]} \\ & \leq \sup_{\|\theta_k\|_2 \leq \widetilde{M}} \sum_{k \in [K]} \sqrt{\sum_{l=1}^d \lambda_l<\theta_k, \varphi_l>^2} \cdot \sum_{k \in [K]} \sqrt{ (\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{l=1}^{d} \frac{1}{\lambda _l} \mathbb{E} [< \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _l>^2])} \\ & + \widetilde{M} \sum_{k \in [K]} \sqrt{\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum_{l > d} \mathbb{E}[ < \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _l>^2 ]} \\ & \leq \sup_{\|\theta_k\|_2 \leq \widetilde{M}} \sum_{k \in [K]} \sqrt{\sum_{l=1}^d \lambda_l<\theta_k, \varphi_l>^2} \cdot \sqrt{K} \sqrt{ \sum_{k \in [K]} (\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{l=1}^{d} \frac{1}{\lambda _l} \mathbb{E} [< \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _l>^2])} \\ & + \widetilde{M} \sqrt{K} \sqrt{ \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum_{l > d} \mathbb{E}[ < \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _l>^2 ]}\\ & \leq \sup_{\|\theta_k\|_2 \leq \widetilde{M}} \sum_{k \in [K]} \sqrt{\sum_{l=1}^d \lambda_l<\theta_k, \varphi_l>^2} \cdot \sqrt{ \left( \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{m_k} \right) \left( \sum_{k \in [K]} \sum _{l=1}^{d} \frac{1}{\lambda _l} \mathbb{E} [< \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _l>^2] \right) } \\ & + \widetilde{M} \sqrt{ \left( \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{m_k} \right) \left( \sum_{k \in [K]} \sum_{l > d} \mathbb{E}[ < \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k), \varphi _l>^2 ] \right) }\\ & \leq \sup_{\|\theta_k\|_2 \leq \widetilde{M}} \sum_{k \in [K]} \sqrt{\sum_{l=1}^d \lambda_l<\theta_k, \varphi_l>^2} \cdot \sqrt{ \left( \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{m_k} \right) \left( \sum _{l=1}^{d} \frac{1}{\lambda _l} \mathbb{E} [< \phi({\mathbf{x}}), \varphi _l>^2] \right) } \\ & + \widetilde{M} \sqrt{ \left( \sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{m_k} \right) \left( \sum_{l > d} \mathbb{E}[ < \phi ({\mathbf{x}}), \varphi _l>^2 ] \right) }. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound by Cauchy-Schwarz across tasks.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since $\sum_{k \in [K]} \sqrt{\sum_{l=1}^d \lambda_l<\theta_k, \varphi_l>^2} \leq \sqrt{r}$, $\mathbb{E} [<\phi({\mathbf{x}}), \varphi_l>^2] = \lambda_l$, then \begin{align*} \mathbb{E} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} (\diamondsuit) \leq \sqrt{\sum _{k \in [K]} \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{m_k} r d } +\widetilde{M} \sqrt{\sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{m_k} \sum_{l > d} \lambda_l }, \end{align*} so $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{F}) \leq \min_{d \geq 0} \sqrt{\sum _{k \in [K]} \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{m_k} r d } +\widetilde{M} \sqrt{\sum_{k \in [K]} \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{m_k} \sum_{l > d} \lambda_l } $.
nodes.statement_short: Plug in the constraints and minimize over $d$.

nodes.name: Reduce to centered class
nodes.statement: We can notice that \begin{align*} \mathcal{R}\{ h \in \mathcal{H}, \mu^2 \mathbb{E} (h_k - h_k^*)^2 \leq r \} & = \mathcal{R}\{ h \in \mathcal{H}, \mathbb{E} (h_k - h_k^*)^2 \leq \frac{r}{\mu ^2} \} = \mathcal{R}\{ h-h^*, h \in \mathcal{H}, \mathbb{E} (h_k - h_k^*)^2 \leq \frac{r}{\mu ^2} \} \\ & \leq \mathcal{R}\{ h - g, h,g \in \mathcal{H}, \mathbb{E} (h_k - g_k^*)^2 \leq \frac{r}{\mu ^2} \} = 2 \mathcal{R}\{ h, h \in \mathcal{H}, \mathbb{E} h_k ^2 \leq \frac{r}{4 \mu ^2} \}, \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the localized class around $h^*$ to twice a centered class.

nodes.name: Sub-root function Psi
nodes.statement: We define a function $\Psi(r) = \frac{\widetilde{c}_1}{2} \mathcal{R}\{ h \in \mathcal{H}, \mu^2\mathbb{E} (h_k - h_k^*)^2 \leq r \}+\frac{11\mu^2 t}{m}$, $\widetilde{c}_1 = 2B\mu$. $\Psi(r)$ is a sub-root function (owing to Lemma~3.4 in \cite{Bartlett_2005}).
nodes.statement_short: Define the sub-root function $\Psi$.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 2
nodes.statement: Then use the Proposition~\ref{thm:kernel upper bound}, we can get \begin{align*} \Psi(r) \leq \sum_{k \in [K]} \left( \frac{2 \chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum_{l=1}^{\infty} \min\{\frac{r}{4 \mu^2},\widetilde{M}^2 \lambda_{kl}\} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}} + \frac{11 \mu^2 t}{m}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\Psi$ using the kernel LFRC bound.

nodes.name: Reduction to a fixed-point inequality
nodes.statement: Similar to \cite{Bartlett_2005} (i.e., adding a constant $c$ to a sub-root function can increase its fixed point by at most $2c$), it suffices to show that \begin{align*} r \leq 2B\mu \sum_{k \in [K]} \left( \frac{2 \chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum_{l=1}^{\infty} \min\{\frac{r}{4\mu^2},\widetilde{M}^2 \lambda_{kl}\} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to bound $r$ satisfying a fixed-point inequality.

nodes.name: Solve the inequality
nodes.statement: Then \begin{align*} r \leq C \left[ \sum_{k \in [K]} \min _{0 \leq d_k \leq m_k} \left( \frac{1}{2 \mu} \sqrt{\frac{r d_k \chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k}} +\widetilde{M} \sqrt{\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{l > d_k} \lambda _{kl}} \right) \right]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Solve for $r$ in terms of eigenvalue tails.

nodes.name: Bound the fixed point
nodes.statement: Since $r \geq \Psi(r)$ and the property in Lemma \ref{lemma:sub-root pro}, i.e., the fixed point $r^*$ satisfied $r^* = \Psi(r^*)$. Then \begin{align*} r ^* \leq C \left[ \sum_{k \in [K]} \min _{0 \leq d_k \leq m_k} \left( \frac{1}{2 \mu} \sqrt{\frac{r d_k \chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k}} +\widetilde{M} \sqrt{\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{l > d_k} \lambda _{kl}} \right) \right], \end{align*} where $C$ is a constant about $B, \mu$.
nodes.statement_short: Use Lemma 1 to transfer the bound to $r^*$.

nodes.name: Reduce to matrix norm constraint
nodes.statement: Similarly, we can get $\mathcal{R}\{ f \in \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{E} f_k^2 \leq r \} = \mathcal{R} \{ f \in \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{E} [{\mathbf{x}}^T \theta_k \theta_k^T {\mathbf{x}}] \leq r \} = \mathcal{R} \{ f \in \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{E} [\| \theta_k \theta_k^T \|] \leq \frac{\sqrt{r}}{\bar{M}} \}$.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the variance constraint as a constraint on $\theta_k\theta_k^T$.

nodes.name: SVD decomposition
nodes.statement: Then we donate the above as $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{F}) = \mathcal{R}(\mathcal{F}_{2,2})$, and consider the SVD composition of $\Theta$, i.e., $\Theta = \sum_{l = 1} u_l v_l^T \widetilde{\lambda}_l $, where ${\{\widetilde{\lambda}_l\}}_{l = 1}^{\infty}$ are the singular values of $\Theta$ and are sorted in a nonincreasing order. Then \begin{align*} & \frac{1}{K} \sum _{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k} \sum _{j \in [J_k]} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta _i <\theta_k, {\mathbf{x}}_i> = \sum_k \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum_{j \in [J_k]} \frac{\omega_{kj}}{\chi_f(G_k)} \sum_{i \in [I_{kj}]} \zeta_i < \theta_k, {\mathbf{x}}_i > \\ = & \sum _{k \in [K]} <\theta_k, \frac{\chi _f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{j \in [J_k]} \frac{\omega_{kj}}{\chi _f(G_k)} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta_i {\mathbf{x}}_i> \\ \leq & \sum _{k \in [K]} <\theta_k, \frac{\chi _f(G_k)}{K m_k} \zeta_k {\mathbf{x}}_k > \\ = & \sum _{k \in [K]} [ <\sum _{l = 1}^{d_k} \sqrt{\lambda _{kl}}<\theta_k, \varphi _{kl}>\varphi _{kl} , \sum _{l = 1}^{d_k} \frac{1}{\sqrt{ \lambda _{kl}}} <\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \zeta_k \phi ({\mathbf{x}}_k) , \varphi _{kl} > \varphi _{kl}> \\ + & <\theta_k, \sum _{l > d_k} <\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \zeta_k {\mathbf{x}}_k, \varphi _{kl} >, \varphi _{kl}>] \\ \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use the SVD of $\Theta$ and split the linear functional.

nodes.name: Bound as in Proposition 4
nodes.statement: Let $\diamondsuit = \frac{1}{K} \sum _{k \in [K]} \frac{1}{m_k}$ $ \sum _{j \in [J_k]} \omega_{kj} \sum _{i \in I_{kj}} \zeta _i <\theta_k, {\mathbf{x}}_i>$, then similar to the proof of Proposition~\ref{thm:kernel compute2}, $\| \sum _{l=1}^{d} u_{l} v_{l}^T \widetilde{\lambda} _{l}^2 \| \leq \frac{\sqrt{r}}{\widetilde{M}}$, we can get \begin{align*} \mathcal{R}\{ f \in \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{E} f_k^2 \leq r \} \leq \sum_k \left( \frac{2 \chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{l = 1} ^{\infty} \min \{ \frac{r}{\bar{M}^2} , \widetilde{M}^2 \widetilde{\lambda} ^2_{l} \} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound as in Proposition 4 to conclude.

nodes.name: Reduce as in Corollary 2
nodes.statement: Similarly, we can prove the Corollary \ref{thm: loss bound computing2} likely the Corollary \ref{thm: loss bound computing}. \begin{align*} \mathcal{R}\{ h \in \mathcal{H}, \mu^2 \mathbb{E} (h_k - h_k^*)^2 \leq r \} & = \mathcal{R}\{ h \in \mathcal{H}, \mathbb{E} (h_k - h_k^*)^2 \leq \frac{r}{\mu ^2} \} = \mathcal{R}\{ h-h^*, h \in \mathcal{H}, \mathbb{E} (h_k - h_k^*)^2 \leq \frac{r}{\mu ^2} \} \\ & \leq \mathcal{R}\{ h - g, h,g \in \mathcal{H}, \mathbb{E} (h_k - g_k)^2 \leq \frac{r}{\mu ^2} \} = 2 \mathcal{R}\{ h, h \in \mathcal{H}, \mathbb{E} h_k ^2 \leq \frac{r}{4 \mu ^2} \}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a centered class as in Corollary 2.

nodes.name: Apply Corollary 1 and Proposition 3
nodes.statement: Owing to the property in Lemma \ref{lemma:sub-root pro}, i.e., the fixed point $r^*$ satisfies $r^* = \Psi(r^*)$, Then we can use the Corollary \ref{thm : Lipschitz bound loss space} and Proposition \ref{thm:linear upper bound} to get the results.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the fixed-point property, Corollary 1 and Proposition 3.

nodes.name: Bound r*
nodes.statement: According to the Proposition \ref{thm:linear upper bound}, \begin{align*} r ^* \leq C \left[ \sum_{k \in [K]} \min _{d_k \geq 0} \left( \frac{1}{2 \mu} \cdot \frac{1}{\bar{M}} \sqrt{\frac{r d_k \chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k}} +\widetilde{M} \sqrt{\frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{l > d_k} \widetilde{ \lambda} _{kl}^2} \right) \right], \end{align*} where $C$ is a constant about $B, \mu$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $r^*$ by singular-value tails.

nodes.name: Shared decomposition
nodes.statement: If we use the second decomposition of $\Theta$, then \begin{align*} r ^* \leq C \sum_k\left[\min _{d \geq 0} \left( \frac{1}{2 \mu} \cdot \frac{1}{\bar{M}} \sqrt{ \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} r d}+\widetilde{M} \sqrt{ \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{l > d} \widetilde{ \lambda} _{l}^2} \right) \right]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use a shared decomposition of $\Theta$.

nodes.name: Final bound on r*
nodes.statement: Furthermore, $r^*$ satisfies \begin{align} r^* \leq \sum_k \min _{d \geq 0} \left( \frac{d}{\bar{M}^2} \frac{\chi_f(G_k) }{K m_k} + \widetilde{M} \sqrt{ \frac{\chi_f(G_k)}{K m_k} \sum _{l >d} \widetilde{ \lambda} _{l}^2} \right). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: State the final bound on $r^*$.

nodes.name: Rewrite empirical AUUC
nodes.statement: From Definition \ref{def:multi own2 auuc}, we know the empirical AUUC of $h$, then \begin{align*} \widehat{AUUC} (h,S) = & \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^K \int_{0}^{1} V(h_k,{\mathbf{x}}) d {\mathbf{x}} \overset{\text{\ding{172}}}{=} \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^K \int_{0}^{1} ( F_{h_k}^{S^T_k}({\mathbf{x}}) - F_{h_k}^{S^C_k}({\mathbf{x}}) ) d {\mathbf{x}} \\ = & \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^K \left( \int_{0}^{1} F_{h_k}^{S^T_k}({\mathbf{x}}) d {\mathbf{x}} + \int_{0}^{1} F_{h_k}^{S^C_k}({\mathbf{x}}) d {\mathbf{x}} \right) \\ \overset{\text{\ding{173}}}{=} & \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k \in [K]} ( \bar{y}_k^T (1-\bar{y}_k^T) \cdot AUC(h_k, S_k^T) + \frac{(\bar{y}_k^T)^2}{2} \\ & - \bar{y}_k^C (1-\bar{y}_k^C) \cdot AUC(h_k, S_k^C) - \frac{(\bar{y}_k^C)^2}{2} ) \\ \overset{\text{\ding{174}}}{=} & \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k \in [K]} ( \bar{y}_k^T (1-\bar{y}_k^T) \cdot AUC(h_k, S_k^T) + \frac{(\bar{y}_k^T)^2}{2} \\ & - \bar{y}_k^C (1-\bar{y}_k^C) \cdot (1 - AUC(h_k, \widetilde{S}_k^C)) - \frac{(\bar{y}_k^C)^2}{2} ) \\ \overset{\text{\ding{175}}}{=} & \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k \in [K]} ( \bar{y}_k^T (1-\bar{y}_k^T) \cdot (1 - \hat{R}_k (h_k, S_k^T)) + \frac{(\bar{y}_k^T)^2}{2} \\ & - \bar{y}_k^C (1-\bar{y}_k^C) \cdot (1 - (1 - \hat{R}_k (h_k, \widetilde{S}_k^C)) - \frac{(\bar{y}_k^C)^2}{2} ) \\ = & \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k = 1}^K ( \underbrace{ \bar{y}_k^T - \frac{1}{2} ((\bar{y}_k^T)^2 + (\bar{y}_k^C)^2) }_{\hat{\gamma}_k^{T,C}} ) - \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^K ( \underbrace{ \bar{y}_k^T (1-\bar{y}_k^T) }_{\lambda_k^T} \hat{R}_k(h_k,S_k^T) \\ & + \underbrace{ \bar{y}_k^C (1-\bar{y}_k^C) }_{\lambda_k^C} \hat{R}_k(h_k,\widetilde{S}_k^C) ) \\ \overset{\text{\ding{176}}}{\geq} & \hat{\Gamma}^{T,C} - \left( \Lambda^T \hat{R}(h,S^T) + \Lambda^C \hat{R}(h,\widetilde{S}^C) \right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite empirical AUUC through cumulative gain, Gini/AUC and ranking risk.

nodes.name: Justify identities
nodes.statement: \text{\ding{172}} is due to \cite{aminiKDD2021uplift_Modeling,KDD2011_Ffunction}, i.e., $F_{h_k}^{S^T_k}({\mathbf{x}}), F_{h_k}^{S^C_k}({\mathbf{x}})$ can be induced by $h$, and $V(h_k,{\mathbf{x}}) = F_{h_k}^{S^T_k}(x) - F_{h_k}^{S^C_k}({\mathbf{x}})$. \text{\ding{173}} is due to \cite{aminiKDD2021uplift_Modeling,KDD2011_ginifunction}, i.e., a relationship between $F_{h_k}^D$, $Gini(h, D)$ and $AUC$, where D represents a dataset. Then we can get $\int_{0}^{1} F_{h_k}^D({\mathbf{x}}) d {\mathbf{x}} = \bar{y}_D (1-\bar{y}_D) \cdot AUC (h,D) + \frac{(\bar{y}_D)^2}{2} $, and then substitute it to \text{\ding{172}}. In \text{\ding{174}}, we revert labels in $S^C_k$ for $\forall k \in [K]$, i.e., $\widetilde{S}_k^C = \{{\mathbf{x}}_{ki},1-y_{ki},C \}_{i=1}^{m_k^C}$. Thus $AUC(h_k,S_k^C) = 1 - AUC (h_k, \widetilde{S_k^C})$ and substitute it to \text{\ding{173}}. Moreover, \text{\ding{175}} is due to the relationship between $AUC$ and empirical ranking risk, i.e., $AUC(h_k,D) = 1-\hat{R}_k(h_k,D)$, where $\hat{R}_k (h_k,D) = \frac{1}{|D^+||D^-|} \sum_{({\mathbf{x}}_{ki},{\mathbf{x}}_{kj}) \in D^+ \times D^-} [\! [h_k({\mathbf{x}}_{ki}) \leq h_k({\mathbf{x}}_{kj})]\!] $. The last inequality \text{\ding{176}} is due to $\sum_{i \in [n]} a_i b_i \leq \sum{i \in [n]} a_i \cdot \sum{i \in [n]} b_i$.

nodes.statement: Finally, we take expectations from both sides, then \begin{align*} AUUC (h) \geq \Gamma^{T,C} - \left( \Lambda^T \mathbb{E}_{S^T} [ \hat{R}(h,S^T) ] + \Lambda^C \mathbb{E}_{S^C} [ \hat{R}(h,\widetilde{S}^C) ] \right). \end{align*}
